question.:question/problem: Compute the rate of change of the function $f(x,y)=x^{2} - 3 y^{2}$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)=⟨- t,t + 3⟩$ at the point $t=2.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The rate of change of $f(x,y)$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)$ is given by $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))].$ To calculate this, we can use the chain rule.

The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}(x^{2} - 3 y^{2}),\frac{∂}{∂y}(x^{2} - 3 y^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2 x,- 6 y⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=- t$, $y=t + 3$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =⟨2 \left(- t\right),- 6 \left(t + 3\right)⟩ \\  & =⟨- 2 t,- 6 t - 18⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t + 3)⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨- 2 t,- 6 t - 18⟩\cdot ⟨-1,1⟩ \\  & =\left(- 2 t\right)\cdot \left(-1\right)+\left(- 6 t - 18\right)\cdot \left(1\right) \\  & =- 4 t - 18.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of change of $f$ along the curve $r(t)$ at $t=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(2))] & =- 4 (2) - 18 \\  & =-26.\end{aligned}
